tasks.short: Coordinate event arrangements and changes with venue staff.

steps.what: Review the event brief, venue agreement and latest schedule.
Write questions and send an agenda to venue staff.

loop.output: Agenda with unresolved questions and source references.
loop.check: Planner checks questions against source passages; dates and quantities retain source values.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing or conflicting facts go to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Correspondence contains free-text requests and qualifications that fixed agenda rules cannot reliably interpret.

steps.what: Discuss room layouts, timings, access and service dependencies with venue staff.
Accept arrangements within authority and refer material changes for approval.
Send confirmed arrangements and update the shared event schedule.

tasks.design: A job assembles current records from the {DOCS}, {CLM} and {PROJECT}, then a bounded drafting loop prepares the coordination agenda. The planner conducts the venue discussion and approves changes within delegated limits; the {WORKFLOW} updates the schedule and sends confirmations through the {EMAIL} only from approved records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Venue correspondence, agreements and schedules sit apart. Human discussion resolves practical dependencies that templates cannot settle.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval flows and small integrations can connect the records. Coding assistance reduces implementation effort; bounded drafting handles correspondence.
tasks.still_hard: Venue access restrictions, changing versions, contractual ambiguities and relationship-sensitive negotiations.
tasks.human_edge: The planner reads hesitation, tests practical trade-offs and secures workable commitments from venue staff.

ambition.what: A venue change-impact brief showing affected timings, costs and responsibilities.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling agendas and repeating confirmations. The planner can present change impacts earlier; spending and contractual authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess how venue changes affect campaign goals and attendee experience.
reach.learn: Campaign objectives, audience priorities and event success measures.

evidence.claim: Approved-record assembly, schedule updates and confirmation routing are suitable for deterministic automation.
Free-text agenda drafting can use a bounded model loop; venue negotiation remains human.

assumptions: The event brief, agreement and schedule have identifiable current versions.
Confirmations communicate approved arrangements without creating new commitments.
Build ranges cover a small reusable workflow for one team.
unknowns: Which system holds the authoritative event schedule?
What changes can the planner approve without sponsor approval?
Are venue contacts permitted recipients of the proposed confirmation content?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the proposed workflow?
research_questions: Does the existing {PROJECT} support approval-triggered schedule updates and external notifications?
Can agenda drafts retain reliable references to source passages?
new_work: Review agenda drafts and resolve source conflicts.
Maintain approval limits, recipient lists and event templates.
Arrange employee consultation under national rules where applicable; the access range includes an initial allowance.

tasks.short: Inspect venues against event requirements and arrange corrections.

steps.what: Prepare an inspection checklist from approved event requirements and venue plans.
Walk the venue, check facilities and record evidence of gaps.
Decide whether requirements are met and identify corrections or specialist checks.
Send findings, assign correction deadlines and request completion evidence.

tasks.design: A checklist generator combines approved requirement fields and inspection templates from the {DOCS} into a form in the {WORKFLOW}. The planner inspects and accepts the venue; approved findings create correction tasks in the {PROJECT} and requests through the {EMAIL}, with closure requiring the specified evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements vary by event, and physical conditions cannot be established from venue documents alone.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable forms, reusable requirement templates and inexpensive record integration reduce preparation and follow-up work.
tasks.still_hard: Physical access, realistic crowd conditions, accessibility details and assessments requiring qualified specialists.
tasks.human_edge: The planner notices practical barriers, tests the space and recognises when specialist assurance is needed.
tasks.altitude: Site visits remain central. Preparation and correction tracking take less time; venue acceptance and specialist sign-off rights do not change.

reach.task: Evaluate venue waste, transport and resource-use evidence.
reach.learn: Evidence quality, measurement boundaries and defensible environmental claims.

evidence.claim: Checklist generation and remediation tracking can use deterministic forms and approval workflows.
Physical inspection and specialist safety assessment cannot be replaced by document processing.

assumptions: Approved requirements can be captured as fields linked to checklist items.
The planner's acceptance concerns event suitability and does not replace statutory certification.
The solution stores findings without assessing employee performance.
unknowns: Which requirements need qualified specialist verification?
Can inspectors capture evidence reliably at venues?
Who can accept residual defects or postpone an event?
What access and employee consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: Can the existing {WORKFLOW} support offline evidence capture and later synchronisation?
Which checklist items require reinspection rather than submitted completion evidence?
new_work: Check that submitted correction evidence supports closure.
Manage evidence access and retention under GDPR.
Confirm consultation needs under national rules; allow further time if formal consultation is required.

tasks.short: Maintain event records, commitments, costs and supporting financial evidence.

steps.what: Read agreements, confirmations and invoices for event details and commitments.

loop.input: Agreements, supplier confirmations and invoices without usable structured data.
loop.output: Proposed commitment fields with source passages and document identifiers.
loop.check: Validate schema, currency, totals and duplicates; planner checks extracted terms and ambiguous amounts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unresolved fields remain unposted.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured feeds are used first; remaining documents express cancellation terms and commitments in varied prose.

steps.what: Retrieve purchase orders, booked costs and payment status for the event.
Update the event ledger and reconcile commitments against actual costs.
Clarify missing evidence, disputed costs and unmatched transactions with finance or suppliers.
Check the event cost summary and confirm outstanding commitments.
File the approved summary and supporting records in the event folder.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration reads the {PROCUREMENT} and {ERP} into an event register on the {DATA_PLATFORM}; a bounded extraction loop proposes fields from remaining documents in the {DOCS} and {CLM}. Deterministic rules reconcile commitments and actuals, feed the {BI}, and route exceptions through the {WORKFLOW}. The planner approves event summaries while financial postings remain subject to the finance team's existing controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event identifiers are inconsistent across financial records, contracts and the planner's {SPREADSHEET}. Unstructured confirmations hide commitments outside booked costs.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations, validated extraction and a shared event identifier can replace repeated entry. Existing financial systems already hold much of the required structured data.
tasks.still_hard: Shared invoices, late credits, changing scope, cancellation liabilities and accounting cut-off decisions.
tasks.human_edge: The planner knows which services were delivered and can explain whether a disputed cost reflects a real commitment.

ambition.what: Recommend weekly contingency reallocations between event cost categories.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from ledger maintenance to resolving material exceptions and explaining the cost outlook. The planner gains earlier information for budget recommendations; spending authority requires separate delegation.

reach.task: Compare event spending with campaign outcomes and future budget options.
reach.learn: Cost allocation, outcome attribution and the limits of event return estimates.

evidence.claim: Financial record assembly, reconciliation and reporting primarily need deterministic integrations and records applications.
Varied agreement prose can require bounded extraction with source checks and human review.
The digest provides no documented event-record automation case supporting a measured saving.

assumptions: The event register is an operational view; the {ERP} remains the financial source of truth.
Automatic register updates use validated source records and preserve an audit trail.
Build ranges cover one finance environment and a limited set of document types.
unknowns: How consistently do transactions carry an event identifier?
Which financial fields and interfaces can the planner access?
Who owns commitment recognition, tax treatment and period cut-off?
What retention periods and employee consultation requirements apply under national rules?
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} reporting provide commitments and actuals without a separate register?
Which source records permit reliable matching without probabilistic inference?
What document sample represents the actual range of supplier terms?
new_work: Review extracted commitments and source conflicts.
Maintain event identifiers, mappings and reconciliation rules.
Monitor failed imports, stale feeds and duplicate records.
Apply GDPR access and retention controls to personal data in supporting documents.
Complete access review and any consultation required under national rules.

tasks.short: Monitor live events, check compliance and participant experience, and resolve problems.

steps.what: Review the response plan, operating conditions and responsibilities before event activity.
Observe event conditions and speak with participants and staff.
Review incoming staff reports and identify issues needing intervention.
Direct responses, reassure participants and escalate safety or compliance problems.
Record incident facts, actions, outcomes and unresolved follow-up.

loop.input: Planner's incident notes, recorded actions and confirmed outcomes.
loop.output: Draft incident record separating facts, reported claims and unresolved points.
loop.check: Planner verifies chronology, identities and outcomes; every factual statement must trace to an input.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; incomplete or sensitive cases use manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative notes need concise synthesis; fixed field copying cannot preserve their qualifications and context.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} assembles an approved monitoring brief from the {DOCS} and collects structured issue reports into a live queue in the {PROJECT}. Configured priority rules and deadlines surface issues while the planner observes conditions and directs responses. A bounded drafting loop prepares incident records for approval without declaring legal compliance or deciding emergency action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Live conditions are situational, and important reports arrive through informal conversations or the {CHAT}. A dashboard cannot establish whether an event is safe or satisfactory.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, queues and notifications can make reported issues visible. Bounded drafting reduces incident paperwork using recorded facts.
tasks.still_hard: Unreported hazards, crowd behaviour, conflicting accounts, emergency response and event-specific legal interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The planner notices distress, de-escalates conflict and acts under uncertainty with responsibility for participants.

ambition.what: Reassign stewards between event zones when queues and assistance requests build.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into chasing reports and writing incident summaries. The planner can adjust steward deployment sooner within existing response authority; emergency and legal decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare accurate participant updates after a material event disruption.
reach.learn: Verified-fact communication, audience needs and escalation for sensitive statements.

evidence.claim: Structured issue queues, deadlines and notifications can support live coordination without autonomous decisions.
Observation, de-escalation and emergency judgement remain human work.
GDPR applies to identifiable incident data; EU AI Act applicability depends on the actual system and use.

assumptions: The response plan and operating conditions are approved by accountable people before use.
Priority rules support attention and do not authorise emergency actions.
Monitoring uses staff reports and observations, without biometric inference or employee scoring.
Rollout includes a live exercise and a fallback communication route.
unknowns: Who has authority to pause activity, evacuate or involve emergency services?
Which permit conditions and national rules apply to each event?
What incident information includes health data or other sensitive personal data?
Does the proposed reporting process require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can the existing {PROJECT} provide reliable mobile issue capture and urgent alerts?
Which issue categories require immediate direct contact regardless of queue status?
What GDPR lawful basis, access restrictions and retention rules fit the incident records?
new_work: Maintain escalation contacts, response rules and approved monitoring briefs.
Review incident drafts and restrict sensitive details.
Check alert delivery and rehearse communication failures.
Tune issue categories after event debriefs.
Assess GDPR and EU AI Act requirements for the actual use, and complete consultation under national rules where applicable.

role.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling records and repeating updates, while site inspection, venue relationships and live response remain central. Better cost and issue visibility supports earlier recommendations; formal spending, safety and contractual authority changes only through delegation.
reach: Marketing manager: connect event spending and operational changes to campaign objectives.
Sustainability specialist: assess venue evidence and environmental claims.
Public relations specialist: communicate verified facts during event disruption.
skills_to_grow: Structured event requirements and shared identifiers.
Accessible venue assessment and specialist escalation.
Incident data protection and clear participant communication.
role.ambitious_version: A planner who brings current cost, venue-change and participant-issue evidence into event decisions, while retaining personal responsibility for relationships and on-site judgement.
